message.reasoning_content:
All 12 workers spawned. Now I wait for their tasks. I'll wait with mode ALL for the 12 task ids, with a timer. But waiting for ALL may be long; let me set a reasonable timer and re-check.

Actually wait conditions with kind 'task' — the instruction says wait on {kind:'task',task_id}. Let me use mode ALL with all 12 conditions plus timer_seconds. Then when it fires, re-check statuses.

Let me set timer to e.g. 300 seconds. But if not all complete, the wait closes on timer. Let me use ANY? ANY would return as soon as one completes, which is inefficient. ALL with timer is better — closes when all settle or timer. Let me do ALL with timer 240.

Hmm, but there's risk workers don't settle. Let me do a first wait with ALL and a good timer. Actually I should be careful: if one worker fails to settle, ALL never satisfies and I just get the timer. That's fine.

Let me wait.
